Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are slowly making their way out to the middle now. Dilara Akter and Shathi Rani are the two openers for Bangladesh Women. Udeshika Prabodani to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Sri Lanka Women, on the other hand, will be disappointed as they could not capitalize on the start that they got. They did lose a couple of wickets early, but the scoring rate was decent as they racked up 49 in the Powerplay. However, things started to slow down when the spinners came in the middle overs, and then they completely lost their way in the end. Harshitha Madhavi played well for her 29, but it was the partnership between Nilakshika Silva and Hasini Perera who top-scored with 43 that got them closer to the 150-run mark. It is still a very good score on this track, and the Lankans will be backing themselves to defend it. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

A fine fightback from Bangladesh Women! They were excellent with the ball, especially at the death where they did not really give anything away. They conceded just 26 runs in the last 5 overs picking up 3 wickets as well. Shorna Akter led the pack with a couple of wickets whereas except for Disha Biswas, every other bowler chipped in with at least one. The pitch looks suited to the spinners as the ball is holding up, but the pacers also got a bit of help with the new ball. Sri Lanka Women will keep that in mind when they come out to defend this target.

Jahanara Alam delivers a slower one, a touch short around off and angling away from the batter, Chamari Athapaththu feels for it and gets a faint tickle to the keeper. Dilara Akter takes the catch and Bangladesh Women have a big breakthrough. The pressure of dot balls telling there!
